claim: Every time any player mills a nonland card, The Wise Mothman triggers: an opponent's radiation mill at the start of their precombat main, Ruin Crab, Mindcrank, The Water Crystal's extra cards. So does Glowing One, once for each nonland card. Put these triggers on the stack as soon as the mill resolves, on the opponent's turn, and target Hancock or Mothman. Don't wait for your own upkeep.
evidence: Game 0008: the auditor logged Mothman or Glowing One triggers never put on the stack on turns 7, 8, 17, 19, 20, 22 and 23. Turn 19 alone was 9 nonland cards: 9 life and counters on three creatures, only recovered late. Game 0031: the Mothman trigger was missed on turns 12, 14, 16 and 17 after each opponent's rad mill. Each had to be caught up in the next upkeep, and one trigger (X=2) came from a mill that happened just before Valefor bounced Mothman.

Game 0052, turns 20 to 29: rad mills on Tidus's, Zuko's and Miirym's turns put a counter on Mothman each time and took him from 3/3 to 12/12. Maddening Cacophony milled 24 cards, but only three counters landed because it had three creatures. On turn 23 an 8-power Mothman killed Elspeth Resplendent before her -7 could make five flying Angels. (Put right by the fact check: Only six of Mothman's nine counters came from opponents' rad mills (turns 20, 21, 22, 26, 28, 29). Three came on its own turns: its own rad mill of Muldrotha (turn 23), Maddening Cacophony (turn 23) and its own rad mill of Mesmeric Orb (turn 27). The opponents' rad mills on turns 24 and 25 hit only lands (Radiant Grove, Raucous Theater) and gave no counter.)

claim: Once Ruin Crab is in play, play your land drop and your land ramp (Nature's Lore, Rampant Growth, Farseek, Cultivate, Evolving Wilds) on the same turn Mothman is out. Each landfall mills every opponent 3, and the nonland cards among those turn into that many +1/+1 counters spread over Mothman, Hancock and the Crab.
evidence: Game 0031, round 4 (turn 15): with Mothman and Hancock already out, the pilot played Tainted Wood and then cast Nature's Lore for Breeding Pool. The two Crab mills hit 6 and 7 nonland cards. Mothman became a 10/10 flier and hit Edgar for 10 commander damage that same turn.

Game 0041: in round 4 the Forest was needed to cast Mothman, so the pilot kept Exotic Orchard back. In round 5 it played the Orchard with Mothman out, and the Crab's mill of Laelia put a counter on both Mothman and the Crab.

claim: When the table has named Mothman as the threat, keep 1GU open for Mutational Advantage and skip a creature to do it. It gives hexproof and indestructible to everything with counters, fizzles targeted exile, and its proliferate grows Mothman and every player's rad counters too.
evidence: Game 0008, round 4: the pilot kept Hancock in hand so Mutational Advantage stayed castable. In round 5, Aragorn aimed Éowyn, Fearless Knight's exile at Mothman. Mutational Advantage countered it by making the target illegal, and Mothman (then on 15 commander damage) killed Aragorn the next turn.

Game 0041: from round 5 on, the pilot left Forest and Temple of Malady untapped for Heroic Intervention. In round 6 Tidus cast Path to Exile on the attacking 17/17 Mothman. Intervention fizzled it, and the hit killed Tidus.

claim: Cast The Water Crystal as soon as opponents are carrying rad counters. It adds four cards to every opponent's radiation mill, so each rad counter turns into more life loss for them, more Mothman counters and more Glowing One life. Infesting Radroach and Glowing One hits then become a finisher.
evidence: Game 0008, round 5: after the Crystal came down, Zuko's rad mill became 11 cards (9 nonland) and took him to 19. In round 7, Radroach gave Ashling 6 rad counters at 2 life, and her next mill of 7+4=11 cards killed her.

claim: Put Mothman's mill counters on Hancock, Ghoulish Mayor whenever you can: each counter on him gives +1/+1 to Mothman, Bloatfly Swarm, Glowing One and every other Zombie or Mutant. Once he has a counter, undying won't bring him back, so keep him out of combat and away from first strikers.
evidence: Game 0031, turn 17: one counter on Hancock made Mothman 11/11. On turn 16, facing Edgar's first-strike vampires, the pilot held Hancock back so it wouldn't lose +2 on Mothman. Game 0008, round 6: Hancock with two counters stayed home while his anthem made the other attackers big enough to kill Zuko.

claim: The Wise Mothman has no vigilance. When you are below about 20 life and an opponent shows a lethal attack (a commander plus a double-strike equipment like Embercleave, plus other attackers), keep Mothman home as a blocker. Attack only with creatures you can spare, and never send Mothman at a player who is at 40 or more when doing so leaves you with no blockers. (Game 0052: at 17 life it sent Mothman at Zuko and the Ambusher at Miirym; on turn 29 Zuko's attack dealt 8+8+4+5 into no blockers and knocked it out from 17.)
evidence: Game 0052, round 7 (turn 27): at 17 life it sent Mothman at Zuko, who was at 45 (Zuko went to 35), and Nightkin Ambusher at Miirym. Embercleave, Heartfire Hero and a Dinosaur token had been on Zuko's side since turn 25. On turn 29 Zuko's attack dealt 8+8+4+5 into no blockers and knocked it out from 18. A 12/12 Mothman blocking Zuko would have taken the 16 double-strike damage. (Put right by the fact check: The seat began round 7 at 18 but its own rad mill on turn 27 (Mesmeric Orb) took it to 17, and it lost nothing more before Zuko's attack; Zuko's first 8 took it to 9. It was knocked out from 17, not 18.)

Game 0062 round 6 (table turn 24): at 40 life it attacked with Mothman (7/7) and the equipped Glowing One to take Zuko from 11 to -1, ending with 0 untapped creatures while Miirym had 5 untapped Dragons. Before its next untap it took 7+7 from two Scourge of Valkas triggers, 6 from Summon: Yojimbo and 17 from Miirym's four attackers, 40 to 6, and died to a third Scourge trigger on turn 27. An 11/11 flying Mothman held back blocks Miirym's 6/6 and survives, and 6 fewer damage would have left it alive.

claim: Tato Farmer untaps only on your own turn. If you tap it on an opponent's turn to take a milled land, it cannot block until your next untap. Take the land only when you don't need Tato as a blocker before your next turn; a 6/9 Tato is worth more than an extra land when you are at 17.
evidence: Game 0052, turn 28 (Tidus's turn): it tapped Tato Farmer to take Overflowing Basin. On turn 29 Zuko attacked and it declared no blocks because all three of its creatures were tapped, then died to 25 damage.

claim: Cast Nuclear Fallout with X=2 before Mothman, not after. The -4/-4 kills a freshly cast 3/3 Mothman along with the opposing early threats. Cast Mothman into the empty board the next turn, and remember the 2 rad counters the Fallout gives each player are milled at each player's next precombat main phase. Mothman gets no counters from those mills unless he is already in play.
evidence: Game 0052, round 4: with six mana, enough for Mothman, it cast Fallout X=2 instead. That killed Terror of the Peaks, Kami of Whispered Hopes, Electro and Headliner Scarlett, and it cast Mothman in round 5. The rad mills on turns 16 to 19 turned up nonland cards (Tidus: Gyre Sage, Kutzil; Zuko: Appa; Miirym: Astral Dragon, Atarka; its own: Ruin Crab, Rampant Growth), but Mothman was not yet in play, so they gave no counters.

claim: Mulligan any opening hand that cannot produce {U} and has nothing to cast before turn three. Keep three lands that between them make B, G and U, or two lands plus Sol Ring / a Talisman / Arcane Signet / Nature's Lore — and note that Exotic Orchard makes only colours an opponent's land can already make, so a hand whose only blue is Exotic Orchard has no blue at all. Game 0062: it cast nothing on its first two turns, got blue only from Breeding Pool on its third turn, and cast The Wise Mothman on its fifth turn (table turn 20) — one to two of its own turns later than the primer's turn 3-4.
evidence: Game 0062: kept 7 after one mulligan with Overgrown Tomb, Swamp, Exotic Orchard, Glowing One, Evolution Sage, Mirelurk Queen, Alpha Deathclaw. The pilot itself wrote on table turn 4 'I still have no blue source for my commander: Exotic Orchard can only make colours my opponents' lands produce, and none of them makes blue yet.' It cast nothing on table turns 4 and 8, got blue only from Breeding Pool on turn 12, and cast The Wise Mothman on turn 20 — four turns later than the primer's turn 3-4 — by which time Miirym had Miirym, Sarkhan, Wrathful Red Dragon and Dragonspeaker Shaman in play. (Put right by the fact check: Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm was not on the battlefield on table turn 20. Miirym cast it from the command zone on table turn 23 ('[turn 23 main1] Miirym casts Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm from Miirym's command'). When this seat cast The Wise Mothman on table turn 20, Miirym's board was Sarkhan, Soul Aflame (turn 15), Wrathful Red Dragon and the re-cast Dragonspeaker Shaman (both turn 19), plus Scaled Nurturer (recast turn 23 — so on turn 20 only Sarkhan, Wrathful Red Dragon and Dragonspeaker Shaman).; THIS SEAT TURN BY TURN records Mothman cast on the seat's round 5 (table turn 20). The primer's 'Cast Mothman on turn 3 or 4' counts the seat's own turns, which were table turns 12 and 16. So the commander landed one to two of its own turns late (four table turns after table turn 16), not four turns later.)

claim: With Mothman out, spare mana is better spent on another body than on equipment: the number of creatures you control caps how widely a big mill's counters can be spread (the trigger hits up to X target creatures, where X is the number of nonland cards milled), and each extra body is also a blocker. With five lands prefer Hancock, Ghoulish Mayor (and a second spell) or Mirelurk Queen over Nuka-Nuke Launcher's {2} plus {3} Equip. Game 0062: Hancock sat in hand from round 1 until the seat died in round 7; on turn 24 the pilot spent all five lands on Launcher plus Equip while Hancock (3), Mirelurk Queen (5) and Evolution Sage (from exile for {2}) were available, and on turn 26 it faced Miirym's attack with no untapped blocker at all.
evidence: Game 0062: Hancock sat in hand from round 1 until the seat died in round 7, never cast. On turn 24, with five lands, the pilot cast Nuka-Nuke Launcher and equipped Glowing One (5 mana) while Hancock (3), Mirelurk Queen (5) and Evolution Sage (recastable from exile for {2}, as its own end note recorded) were all available. Two turns later Miirym milled two nonland cards and Mothman's trigger had only two legal targets — Mothman and Glowing One — for a total of 4 counters, and the seat had no untapped blocker at all. (Put right by the fact check: THE LIST gives the trigger as 'put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to X target creatures, where X is the number of nonland cards milled this way' — X is set by the mill, not by your creature count, and the targets need not be creatures you control. On table turn 26 exactly two nonland cards were milled (Rampant Growth, Sarkhan's Triumph), so X was 2 and the trigger could choose at most two creatures anyway; the seat's two creatures were not a limit there, and extra bodies would have added no counters on that trigger (each of Mothman and Glowing One got 2 via Hardened Scales, 4 in all).)
